steps.name: Prerank GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark sets
caveats: de_results.csv is derived from 6 vs 6 unpaired samples with sample_01 having ~4x below-median library size, already reflected in the DESeq2 stats — no re-normalization needed here since this step consumes the DE table, not raw counts
Do not re-run differential expression; this step starts strictly from the existing de_results.csv per the research question
Gene symbol matching between de_results.csv and the Hallmark GMT (HGNC symbols) must be case/format checked; report unmatched gene count rather than silently dropping
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets are significantly enriched (up or down) in the atopic dermatitis lesional vs control skin DESeq2 contrast already computed in de_results.csv?
acceptance_criteria: Loads /eval-four-models-without-python-enrichment-only-1/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv (12000 genes x 8 columns) and drops rows with missing gene symbol or pvalue/log2_fold_change before ranking

Builds a single ranking metric per gene (e.g. sign(log2_fold_change) * -log10(pvalue), or the Wald stat column if present), deduplicates gene symbols by keeping the entry with the largest |stat|, and confirms >=90% of ranked gene symbols overlap the Hallmark gene set universe before proceeding
Runs gseapy.prerank using the human MSigDB Hallmark GMT staged under /mnt/refs (h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt, 50 sets, HGNC symbols) with default or documented gene_sets_min/max size filters
Outputs a full results table (all 50 Hallmark sets, NES, p-value, FDR q-value, leading-edge genes) sorted by FDR, saved as CSV
Flags sets significant at FDR < 0.05 explicitly in the output and reports how many pass
Produces a plot (e.g. dot plot or barplot of NES for top up/down enriched sets) saved to disk
If the Hallmark GMT is unavailable at run time, the step reports that explicitly rather than silently returning an empty result

plan.title: Hallmark pathway enrichment: AD lesional vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The DESeq2 results table (12000 x 8: gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2_fold_change_se, stat, pvalue, padj, and one more column) for the treated (AD lesional) vs control skin contrast already exists, so no re-analysis of counts is needed. The single remaining analytical question is which of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets are enriched in this contrast. We run a pre-ranked GSEA (fgsea-style, via gseapy prerank in Python per the user's constraint) on genes ranked by a signed statistic (sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue), with the Wald stat as a fallback ranking metric) against the human Hallmark GMT staged in refs. A single enrichment step is sufficient given the existing DE table; results are reported as a ranked table of NES, p-value, and FDR q-value per hallmark set, with plots for the top up/down sets.
